page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highmem-4 is a memory-optimized server instance powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8581C processor. Operating on the x86_64 architecture, this instance features 4 virtual CPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is configured with 31.0 GB of system memory, yielding 7.75 GB of RAM per vCPU. The processor runs at a clock speed of 2.3 GHz and includes a 260 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. This instance does not include local storage or integrated GPUs.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-core capabilities, with Geekbench single-core and text processing scores reaching top-tier classifications. Single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression also demonstrate strong performance. However, multi-core performance is more limited, with stress-ng multi-core and Passmark CPU scores falling into the lower percentiles. Memory bandwidth is relatively constrained, with uncached large-block reads at 32.39 GB/sec and writes at 20.69 GB/sec. The CPU features advanced instruction sets, including Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), which support workloads like low-latency text processing and small-scale LLM inference.

Given the high memory-to-vCPU ratio and strong single-threaded execution, the c4-highmem-4 is suited for memory-intensive applications that do not require massive parallel compute scaling. Appropriate workloads include text processing, single-threaded data compression, static web serving, and lightweight language model inference. The primary tradeoff is the lower multi-core efficiency and moderate memory bandwidth, making it less optimal for heavy multi-threaded database operations or high-throughput Redis deployments.
